analysis:
Examined the new continuation implementation, scheduler patch, file metadata and supplied BASE context. LoopExitThinkingContinuation.swift:108-145 holds the loop-stop terminal, bounds continuation output by remaining budget, and checks cancellation before and after submission. Lines 147-204 combine usage with the original prompt count and injected marker; lines 217-230 serialize cancellation against continuation start. MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:1024-1035 disables continuation for distributed pairs, while 1108-1169 reuses the request, sampling overrides, cache scope, cache enablement and donation demand, waits up to five seconds for row release, and wraps both rows in the existing deadline-checked output stream. No supported cache-isolation regression (T-041), plaintext transport change (T-008), key/attestation change or privileged execution surface is visible.
Material integration questions remain, not findings: verify GenerationLoopGuardPolicy excludes constrained/tool requests or that continuation preserves their enforcement, because the new submission does not pass the original tokenConstraint; verify EngineV2Bridge.submitTokenized rechecks serving authorization, reservation/hold admission and context/resource limits for the longer re-prefill (T-053, T-059, A-018); verify waitForRowRelease and submit terminate promptly on cancellation (T-010). Check usage-signal and terminal consumers against the combined counts, and confirm interpolated submission/event errors at LoopExitThinkingContinuation.swift:141,192 cannot contain prompt content when logged through the new scheduler outcome logger (A-001). Those implementations and the exit-policy eligibility rules are outside this supplied source scope; their absence is not evidence of a missing control.
